title: Set Emplace
description: Construct element in-place in a set
explanation: Emplace constructs the element directly in the set, avoiding a temporary copy.
code:
set<pair<int,int>> st;
st.emplace(1, 2);   // constructs pair in-place

title: Set Emplace Hint
description: Construct in-place with a position hint for efficiency
explanation: Providing a correct hint makes insertion amortized O(1) instead of O(log n).

title: Set Extract C++17
description: Extract a node from a set without copying (C++17)
explanation: Extracts the element as a node handle, allowing modification of the value and moving between sets without copying.

title: Set Merge C++17
description: Transfer elements from one set to another (C++17)
explanation: Transfers all non-duplicate elements from one set into another without copying or moving.

title: Set Equal Range
description: Get range of elements matching a key
explanation: Returns a pair of iterators covering the range of elements equal to the given value (useful for multiset).

title: Set Key Comparison Object
description: Access the set's internal comparison function
explanation: key_comp and value_comp return the comparison object used by the set to order elements.

title: Set With Custom Comparator
description: Use a custom ordering for set elements
explanation: Ordered sets can use custom comparators for descending order or custom sorting logic.

title: Multiset Declaration
description: Declare a multiset that allows duplicate elements
explanation: multiset is like set but allows multiple elements with the same value.

title: Set Difference With Algorithms
description: Compute set difference, intersection, union using STL algorithms
explanation: STL algorithms for sorted ranges can operate on sets to compute union, intersection, difference.

title: Set Std Erase C++20
description: Erase elements by value from a set (C++20)
explanation: C++20 provides free-function std::erase and std::erase_if for all standard containers.

title: MultiSet Erase One Element
description: Erase a single occurrence from multiset
explanation: Using an iterator erases one occurrence; using a value erases ALL occurrences.

title: Unordered Set vs Set Tradeoffs
description: Compare unordered_set vs set performance characteristics
explanation: unordered_set: O(1) average lookup, no ordering, higher memory. set: O(log n), ordered, lower memory.
